0.0.n: The speaker refers to herself or himself with this neutral, polite pronoun.

0.1.n: Marks 私 as the topic of the story.

0.2.n: In そうですね, this helps the speaker pause and gather their thoughts.

0.3.n: Makes the hesitation phrase そうですね polite.

0.4.n: Softens そうですね into a reflective pause rather than a firm statement.

0.6.n: The place graduated from; the usual particle を is omitted in this casual speech.

0.7.n: The て-form of 卒業する connects graduation to what happened next.

1.0.n: Points to the work being discussed and directly modifies 仕事.

1.1.n: Refers to the job or kind of work the speaker wanted to do.

1.2.n: Marks この仕事 as what the speaker wants to do.

1.3.n: する becomes したい to express the speaker's desire.

1.4.n: Casual form of という, introducing the content of the request.

1.5.n: In っていうふうに, frames the preceding words as how the request was expressed.

1.6.n: Turns ふう into a description of how the speaker asked.

1.7.n: 父 is the usual humble way to refer to your own father when speaking to others.

1.8.n: Marks the father as the person receiving the request.

1.9.n: Short for お願いしていた, describing a request made over a past period.

1.10.n: Short for の; adds background explanation before です.

1.11.n: Adds politeness to the explanatory んです construction.

1.12.n: Sets up a contrast with the father's response in the next line.

2.0.n: Modifies 簡単 to indicate a degree: not that easily.

2.1.n: Combines with に to describe how readily the request might be accepted.

2.2.n: Turns 簡単 into a description of how something happens.

2.3.n: Emphasizes そう簡単に, implying that acceptance would not come so readily.

2.6.n: Literally one's own home or group; here it refers to the father's workplace or business.

2.7.n: Marks where the work takes place.

2.8.n: 仕事 combines with する to make a verb.

2.9.n: Turns うちで仕事する into something that can serve as the sentence topic.

2.10.n: Marks working at the family workplace as the topic of the father's warning.

2.11.n: Modifies 甘い世界, referring to an overly easy picture of the work.

2.12.n: Literally sweet, but here suggests something undemanding or forgiving.

2.13.n: Refers figuratively to the professional environment, not the whole planet.

2.14.n: Casual contraction of では; combines with ない to deny the description.

2.15.n: Completes じゃない, rejecting the idea that this is an easy environment.

2.16.n: Adds emphasis to the father's warning.

2.18.n: Casual という introduces the quoted words as the form the father's response took.

2.19.n: Here 形 refers to the manner of the response, not a physical shape.

2.20.n: Links the father's response to the next part of the story.

3.0.n: Here suggests getting some experience first, before trying again.

3.1.n: Combines with 勉強 to refer to learning about life and work in the wider world.

3.2.n: In 社会勉強, means gaining real-world experience rather than classroom study.

3.3.n: Marks 社会勉強 as the activity performed with する.

3.4.n: The て-form of する connects gaining experience with the following events.

4.0.n: Contrasts the outside experience with the speaker's continuing desire to do this work.

4.1.n: Shows that the original desire remained or strengthened despite the intervening experience.

4.2.n: Points back to the previously mentioned wish to do this work.

4.3.n: Here refers specifically to wanting to pursue this job.

4.4.n: Marks その気持ち as what became stronger.

4.5.n: 強い changes to 強く before なる to express becoming strong.

4.6.n: Past form of なる, describing a change in the speaker's desire.

4.7.n: Presents the stronger desire as the reason for applying again.

4.9.n: Indicates another attempt after the earlier request.

4.10.n: Combines with the following して to mean volunteering or putting oneself forward.

4.11.n: Parse as 志願して plus やり始めた, not してやる; 始めた adds started to やる.

4.12.n: Casual という introduces a summary of how the speaker came to start working.

4.13.n: In っていう形で, summarizes how events unfolded rather than describing a physical shape.

4.14.n: Leaves the summary softly open-ended, a common conversational ending.

5.0.n: Sets the time frame for reflecting on how long the speaker has worked.

5.1.n: Marks the present time as the topic.

5.2.n: Emphasizes how much time has passed.

5.3.n: This digit belongs to １２; read the two digits together as twelve.

5.4.n: The split cuts through １２年; together, the preceding １ and this segment mean twelve years.

5.5.n: Includes the stated number: １２年以上 means at least twelve years.

5.6.n: Polite form of 経つ, used for elapsed time; the present form naturally describes the duration reached now.

5.7.n: Softens the reflection and invites the listener to share the sense of elapsed time.

6.0.n: An exclamation expressing impressed surprise at the length of time.

6.1.n: This mark lengthens the preceding vowel, making the reaction more expressive.

0.lit: As for me, well, after graduating university,
0.tip: そうですね can be a thinking pause, not simply agreement.

1.lit: I was asking my father, in the way of saying I want to do this work, but,
1.tip: してた is conversational shorthand for していた, describing a past ongoing action.

2.lit: Not that easily—in the form of saying, Working here isn't that kind of easy world, you know,
2.tip: そう簡単には leaves not so easily implied before shifting into the father's quoted warning.

3.tip: 社会勉強 means gaining practical life experience, not studying social studies.

4.lit: But after all, that desire became stronger, so I applied once again and started doing it—that's how.
4.tip: やり始めた means started doing; the preceding して belongs to 志願して, applied and.

5.lit: Now, already twelve years or more pass, you know.
5.tip: Read １ and ２年 together as １２年; 以上 includes twelve, not just amounts beyond it.

6.tip: The long vowel mark stretches the exclamation to convey stronger surprise.
